columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Vertical 9:16 videos, 3–60 seconds, sound-on by default, in Facebook app, Watch, and News Feed.
Reels can appear on any user’s feed, not just followers; Meta has been pushing Reels hard for organic reach.
Placement in Facebook Watch supports switching between Reels and longer video.

strengths.title: Strong organic reach right now
strengths.detail: Creators often report higher organic reach from Reels than standard posts while Meta boosts the format.

strengths.title: Access to Meta’s dual graph
strengths.detail: Taps both social connections and interest-based discovery, similar to TikTok’s For You.

strengths.title: Easy reuse of existing short-form content
strengths.detail: TikTok/Instagram Reels can be repurposed with minor adjustments, similar vertical format and length.

strengths.title: Bridge between short-form and long-form
strengths.detail: Can funnel viewers into longer videos, Pages, Groups, and events.

weaknesses.title: Dependent on Meta’s algorithmic priorities
weaknesses.detail: Current boost may shift; organic reach could decline if Meta de-emphasizes Reels.

weaknesses.title: Platform clutter and context
weaknesses.detail: Reels compete with ads, posts, and group content, busier than dedicated short-form apps.

weaknesses.title: Monetization still evolving
weaknesses.detail: Reels monetization is expanding but less mature/transparent than YouTube’s Partner Program.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Facebook Reels is meta short-form video on Facebook, Reels discovery and creator monetization. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Facebook Reels are short, vertical videos (3–60 seconds) that appear across Facebook surfaces, designed for engaging, sound-on, trend-focused content with broad organic reach. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Facebook Reels side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Facebook Reels you can use Short-form video and Memberships as first-class product jobs. The job is reach, trends, and native social distribution.

Using Kahana with Facebook Reels

You can use both. Facebook Reels keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep posting on Facebook Reels for reach. Repurpose the clips that should last: turn a series into a hub, or point your bio and pinned comment at a Kahana profile. You can grow an audience on Kahana as well as on the feed.
